title: Torres's Extra-Time Strike Crowns Spain World Cup Champions Over Argentina
excerpt: Substitute Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the 106th minute as Spain beat a toothless Argentina 1-0 to claim their second World Cup title.
body:
• Substitute Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute to give Spain a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium
  • Argentina failed to register a single shot on target in 90 minutes — a first in World Cup final history — before Enzo Fernández was sent off in stoppage time
  • Lamine Yamal, 19, became the youngest player ever to win both the European Championship and the World Cup
  • Spain are now unbeaten in 38 consecutive matches across all competitions, a record for any European or South American nation

A Final That Needed Rescuing

Spain climbed to the summit of world football on Sunday, but they had to drag the World Cup final up there with them. Substitute Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute to prise the trophy from holders Argentina with a 1-0 victory — a result that crowned a new era of Spanish dominance while delivering precious little beauty.

The biggest prize in football deserved a classic. Instead, the world's two finest teams produced a suffocating stalemate that drifted toward penalties before Torres, introduced from the bench alongside Nico Williams and Pedri, finally broke through with Spain's 20th attempt on goal.

Lamine Yamal whipped in a cross from the right, Williams headed it back across goal, and Torres rifled a shot into the top corner past Argentina's Emiliano Martínez. The MetLife Stadium erupted.

"It was a goal scored by 47 million people — it wasn't even mine or from the 26 players. It was destined to happen; it was meant to be a winner."

— Ferran Torres, World Cup final goalscorer

Argentina's Historic Futility

Argentina became the first team in World Cup final history to fail to muster a single shot on target across 90 minutes. Their approach appeared designed to frustrate and disrupt rather than attack, with shirt-pulling, tactical fouls, and time-wasting replacing the flair that had carried them through the knockout rounds.

Lionel Messi, the second player after Brazilian great Cafu to feature in three World Cup finals, was a pale shadow of the player who had orchestrated a stunning semi-final comeback against England. The 39-year-old's likely farewell to the biggest stage ended not with a flourish but in frustration, as Argentina's plan to grind Spain into a penalty shootout fell apart in extra time.

Enzo Fernández's dismissal for a second yellow card — for flattening teenager Pau Cubarsí in stoppage time — capped a dismal afternoon for the holders. The final whistle triggered a brawl as Argentina's frustrations boiled over, with players from both sides pushing and shoving before officials restored order.

Yamal Makes History

While Torres delivered the decisive moment, the tournament belonged to 19-year-old Lamine Yamal. The Barcelona winger became the youngest player in history to win both the European Championship and the World Cup, adding to the continental title he claimed at just 17 in Germany two years ago.

Eight Barcelona players featured in Spain's squad — Joan Garcia, Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsí, Gavi, Pedri, Dani Olmo, Torres, and Yamal — the largest contingent from any single club at the tournament.

Spain's coach Luis de la Fuente, 65, became the oldest manager to win the World Cup. His team have now won every major trophy available to them — the European Championship and the World Cup — while extending their unbeaten run to 38 consecutive matches, a record for any European or South American nation.

The Messi Era Ends

For millions of Indian football fans who have followed Messi's career with devotion, the result marks the likely end of Argentina's golden era. Messi's collection of two Copa América titles and the 2022 World Cup represented one of football's greatest late-career runs, but Sunday's defeat suggested the torch has definitively passed.

Nearly two million fans lined Madrid's streets on Monday to welcome Spain's champions home. In Barcelona, the celebrations were doubly sweet — eight of the 23-man squad call Camp Nou home.

"I'm very moved," de la Fuente told reporters. "We've won everything, absolutely everything, with this generation of players."
